title: Hierarchy
description: What an app built with SimMirror's debug SDK answers to GET /v1/hierarchy?max_nodes=<n> on 127.0.0.1:<port>, sent with Authorization: Bearer <secret>: its views as it sees them, with a label worked out for each. Every other answer is an ErrorBody.

protocol.description: The app SDK protocol version the app speaks.

modal.description: What the app presents in front of the rest, if anything. What it hides is already left out of windows.

keyboard.description: Where the software keyboard is, while it shows. Views under it cannot be reached.

windows.description: The app's windows on screen, the key window first, then from the front to the back.

truncated.description: Whether views were left out to stay within max_nodes or the size limit.

node_count.description: How many nodes the windows hold.

capture_ms.description: How long the app took to walk its views.

notes.description: What the app could not read the way it meant to, such as SwiftUI's debug data being unavailable.

active.description: Whether the app is in front. An app that is not answers 409 instead.

Screen.description: The screen the frames are measured on, in points, held upright.

Orientation.description: Which way up the app's interface is.

Frame.description: Where something is, in points on the screen held upright -- the space accessibility frames use -- whichever way the interface is turned.

Modal.description: Something presented in front of the rest of the app.

name.description: Its title, when it has one.

level.description: The window's level: a larger one is in front.

key.description: Whether it is the key window.

Node.description: A view, or a SwiftUI view, the app found worth saying: what it is, what it says and where it is.

label.description: What it says, worked out by the app: its accessibility label, else its title or text, the text inside it, its image's name, its identifier, or its type's name.

label_source.description: Where the label came from; null when there is none.

value.description: Its value, such as a field's text or a switch's 1 or 0. Always null for a secure field.

interactive.description: Whether a touch on it does something: a control, or a view with a tap gesture.

type_name.description: The UIKit class or SwiftUI view type it was read from.

Kind.description: What a node is, in the words a snapshot uses. Read as open: a receiver reads a kind it does not know as an element with no role.

Trait.description: A state worth saying: selected, or being edited.

NodeSource.description: What the node was read from: a UIKit view, SwiftUI's debug data, or a .simMirror tag the developer put on a view.

ErrorBody.description: Every answer but a hierarchy: 400 bad_request, 401 unauthorized (checked before anything else), 404 not_found, 405 method_not_allowed, 409 inactive, 431 headers_too_large, 503 busy, 507 too_large.

ErrorCode.description: Why a request was not answered with a hierarchy.
